messages:
jen: Heads-up — planning to publish py/ts SDK 2.0 canary tonight during the quiet window (00:30-01:30 UTC). Major: sync client removed, minor API tweaks. Need final +1s and any blocker callouts.

samir: +1 from infra. Verified canary infra capacity and staging pool. Will watch logs.

deploy-bot: [deploybot] scheduling canary publish job: job_id=canary-2024-11-03-01 run_at=2024-11-03T00:45:00Z

rachel: Quick checklist: pip credentials rotated? twine config? npm 2fa tokens? Also update release notes draft in docs repo.

jen: pip creds rotated yesterday (jen@ops did). npm 2FA still on my laptop, will push OTP to 1Password session. Release notes draft: https://git.company/docs/sdk-release-notes/2.0-draft (please add callouts).

marc: small ask — pin old sync client as `@example/sdk@1.x` in our internal examples repo for 30 days with a deprecation note. Avoids breakage for customers copying examples.

samir: Agreed. I'll push a dist-tag `legacy` to npm for 1.x and add a note to pip packaging that 1.x remains available under `example-sdk==1.*` for 30d.

jen: Rollback criteria: smoke tests failing >1 route OR publish fails checksum/signature OR >10% of canary requests error out over 10m. If hit, we abort canary and call a rollback. Who triggers?

marc: I'll be primary to trigger rollback. samir is backup. Postmortem owner: rachel.

release-manager-bot: [release-manager] canary run configured with health probes: /health, /v1/generate smoke, success_rate_threshold=0.9, duration=10m

deploy-bot: job started: canary-2024-11-03-01 -> publishing packages to npm and PyPI. Logs: 
```
> npm publish dist/example-sdk-2.0.tgz --tag canary
> twine upload dist/example_sdk-2.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

jen: Watching logs. Will verify changelog and deprecation blurb.

deploy-bot: publish log: npm ok, twine ok, both artifacts signed. Canary traffic ramp to 5% started.

samir: smoke-run 1m: 98% success, latencies nominal.

rachel: added deprecation blurb to release notes: "Sync client removed — see migration guide at /migrate-sync-to-async". Also flagged SDK breaking changes in docs index.

marc: thumbs up. If nothing else in next 30m we can promote to staged.

(00:58 UTC) deploy-bot: alert: smoke-run window 10m ended; error_rate=0.12 (12%). Condition breached. Marking canary as at-risk.

jen: Noted — what errors? stack traces or 500 spikes?

samir: Quick grep of logs shows repeated 503s from worker pool on long prompts: "KV cache OOM" appearing ~3x in a minute. Might be runtime memory handling regression with new runtime kernel.

marc: Hold promotion. Rollback plan: unpublish canary tag and remove PyPI wheel from canary index; revert dist-tag to previous stable for traffic routing, and open hotfix branch. I will trigger.

marc: Actioning rollback now. deploy-bot: please stop ramp and revert traffic and remove canary tags.

deploy-bot: rollback actions initiated:
- npm dist-tag remove example-sdk@2.0 canary
- npm dist-tag add example-sdk@1.9.4 latest
- PyPI: mark 2.0 yanked from canary index (internal mirror)
- traffic: ramp down to 0%

(01:03 UTC) deploy-bot: rollback complete. Canary artifacts still in central registries (can't fully un-publish), but traffic reverted.

jen: Thanks. Next steps: samir to open infra/regression issue referencing kernel change and KV cache OOM; marc to push pin/legacy tags in examples; rachel to finalize release notes but mark release on hold. We will triage tomorrow morning (08:00 UTC).

samir: Filed issue: https://issues.company/INFRA-5421 "KV cache OOM regressions on 2.0 runtime kernels" with diagnostics and sample traces. Assigned to eng-runtime.

rachel: Release notes updated -> status: on_hold. Will add a short blurb for customers who grabbed canary accidentally.

marc: Deploy postmortem owner pre-assigned to rachel. We'll reconvene 08:00 UTC. Thanks folks :handshake:

jen: Excellent — closing thread for now. Keep any follow-ups in the ticket.
